annotationNotes: Original synthetic diagnostic scenarios, labeled by the implementation author. No independent annotation or real-world accuracy claim. Reserved split is visible source, not an independently held-out benchmark. Gold PageRepresentations isolate analysis; HTML is reserved for extraction evaluation in Phase 3.

blocks.text: Grocery parcels run out before payday

The neighborhood pantry has reduced each family's grocery parcel because demand has doubled. Parents skip dinner so their children can eat. A nutrition leaflet mentions diabetes, but the request is for donated staples and reliable access to food, not clinical treatment.

expected.rationale: The neighborhood pantry has reduced each family's grocery parcel because demand has doubled.

blocks.text: The kitchen is closed on Sundays

When the community kitchen shuts for the weekend, residents without money for groceries have no dependable meal. Volunteers want funding for seven-day service. The discussion concerns filling empty cupboards and keeping people fed, rather than choosing a healthier diet.

expected.rationale: When the community kitchen shuts for the weekend, residents without money for groceries have no dependable meal.

blocks.text: Where do children eat during the break?

Families who rely on school lunches cannot replace those meals during the holidays. A local charity is arranging grocery vouchers and pickup points. Its organizers are asking neighbors to help prevent children going hungry while classes are closed.

expected.rationale: Families who rely on school lunches cannot replace those meals during the holidays.

blocks.text: Benefits arrived after the cupboards emptied

Households report that delays in their food benefit renewals left them unable to buy groceries for weeks. The agency has offered a review meeting. Residents want emergency food assistance while their cases are processed and the recurring backlog is fixed.

expected.rationale: Households report that delays in their food benefit renewals left them unable to buy groceries for weeks.

blocks.text: A small raise, a much larger loss

An increase of a few dollars in monthly income ended a family's cash assistance. Their remaining earnings cannot cover essentials. Residents want the eligibility rules reviewed so taking a little extra work does not deepen material hardship.

expected.rationale: An increase of a few dollars in monthly income ended a family's cash assistance.

blocks.text: Neighbors ask for a basic income floor

A municipal pilot would provide monthly cash support to residents living below the poverty line. Participants describe choosing which essential bill to leave unpaid. The council is inviting comments on whether the program should continue next year.

expected.rationale: A municipal pilot would provide monthly cash support to residents living below the poverty line.

blocks.text: The town's biggest employer is leaving

The only large factory in the area is closing, eliminating hundreds of jobs. Residents have asked for retraining and help finding work before unemployment benefits run out. The immediate concern is securing replacement employment, not negotiating conditions at the closed plant.

expected.rationale: The only large factory in the area is closing, eliminating hundreds of jobs.

blocks.text: Qualified applicants cannot find a way back

People who have been out of work for more than a year say employers discard their applications. A public employment program proposes paid placements to help them return. Its consultation asks which hiring barriers prevent residents from obtaining jobs.

expected.rationale: People who have been out of work for more than a year say employers discard their applications.

blocks.text: Hours worked disappear from the pay slip

Restaurant staff say their employer regularly deletes the last hour of each shift from their recorded time. They want the labor agency to recover wages already earned. No union negotiation is described; the issue is missing pay and enforcement of payment rules.

expected.rationale: Restaurant staff say their employer regularly deletes the last hour of each shift from their recorded time.

blocks.text: A proposed floor under hourly pay

The state legislature is considering an increase in the minimum wage. Workers say full-time earnings do not cover essentials, while employers have raised concerns about implementation. A hearing will examine the proposed pay rate and enforcement responsibilities.

expected.rationale: The state legislature is considering an increase in the minimum wage.

blocks.text: Essentials keep taking more of each paycheck

Electricity, heating fuel and groceries have all become more expensive, while household incomes have barely changed. Residents are seeking a public review of charges and targeted help with essential bills. The article does not focus on housing or medical treatment.

expected.rationale: Electricity, heating fuel and groceries have all become more expensive, while household incomes have barely changed.

blocks.text: Keeping basic purchases within reach

A consumer group proposes temporary rebates for essential household purchases after a sharp rise in prices. Parents describe cutting back on several everyday necessities. The public discussion is about purchasing power and household living costs across the community.

expected.rationale: A consumer group proposes temporary rebates for essential household purchases after a sharp rise in prices.

blocks.text: The same qualifications, different answers

An audit submitted identical job applications with names associated with different racial groups. Black applicants received far fewer interview invitations. Residents are calling for equal-treatment enforcement; the report is about discriminatory selection rather than a general shortage of jobs.

expected.rationale: An audit submitted identical job applications with names associated with different racial groups.

blocks.text: Different treatment at the public counter

Black residents report being asked for documents that white neighbors are not required to provide for the same municipal service. Organizers want an independent equality review. The article centers on race-based treatment by staff and does not discuss medical services.

expected.rationale: Black residents report being asked for documents that white neighbors are not required to provide for the same municipal service.

blocks.text: A membership rule with unequal consequences

A publicly supported recreation center repeatedly rejects applications from an ethnic minority while accepting otherwise equivalent applications from other residents. Community members are seeking enforcement of equal access. They describe a discriminatory barrier, not a debate about exercise or health advice.

expected.rationale: A publicly supported recreation center repeatedly rejects applications from an ethnic minority while accepting otherwise equivalent applications from other residents.

blocks.text: Apprenticeships advertised to everyone, offered to men

Women applying to a public apprenticeship program say staff told them the placements were for men. They met the published requirements. The complaint asks the program to end gender-based exclusion and assess applicants on the same terms.

expected.rationale: Women applying to a public apprenticeship program say staff told them the placements were for men.

blocks.text: Only fathers are described as committed

A workplace review finds mothers were routinely rejected for promotion despite the same experience and performance as fathers. Employees have asked for equal-treatment protections. The story concerns discriminatory judgments about gender and parenthood, not a proposal for medical benefits.

expected.rationale: A workplace review finds mothers were routinely rejected for promotion despite the same experience and performance as fathers.

blocks.text: The consultation has a staircase at the door

Residents using wheelchairs cannot enter the venue selected for a public hearing. The organizer declined to move the meeting or provide an accessible alternative. The complaint seeks equal participation for disabled residents, not treatment of their disabilities.

expected.rationale: Residents using wheelchairs cannot enter the venue selected for a public hearing.

blocks.text: A public service without a way to communicate

Deaf residents say the municipal advice service refuses to provide sign-language interpretation. They cannot obtain the same information as hearing residents. Advocates want reasonable accommodations and equal access to the service, without making assumptions about medical needs.

expected.rationale: Deaf residents say the municipal advice service refuses to provide sign-language interpretation.

blocks.text: An online form that screen readers cannot use

Blind residents cannot submit a required municipal application because its controls have no accessible labels. They are asking the agency to provide an accessible route and fix the form. The central problem is equal access to a public service.

expected.rationale: Blind residents cannot submit a required municipal application because its controls have no accessible labels.

blocks.text: One set of rules for different couples

A publicly funded family service accepts different-sex couples but turns away same-sex couples with the same circumstances. Residents have filed an equality complaint. They want the service offered on equal terms rather than a separate program.

expected.rationale: A publicly funded family service accepts different-sex couples but turns away same-sex couples with the same circumstances.

blocks.text: Residents challenge an exclusion based on identity

A municipal facility has announced that transgender residents cannot use services matching their gender identity. Those affected are seeking nondiscrimination protections. The article examines exclusion from public life; it does not discuss clinical treatment or medical diagnoses.

expected.rationale: A municipal facility has announced that transgender residents cannot use services matching their gender identity.

blocks.text: An accommodation offered selectively

Workers say requests to observe one religious holiday are routinely accepted while comparable requests from another faith are refused. They seek equal consideration and reasonable accommodations. The disagreement concerns religious discrimination, not a general proposal for paid leave.

expected.rationale: Workers say requests to observe one religious holiday are routinely accepted while comparable requests from another faith are refused.

blocks.text: The same room, a different rule

A council-owned meeting room is available to community groups, but officials rejected an otherwise eligible group because of its religion. Residents are asking for equal access. The issue is exclusion on religious grounds rather than the content of the group's beliefs.

expected.rationale: A council-owned meeting room is available to community groups, but officials rejected an otherwise eligible group because of its religion.

blocks.text: Working full time and still priced out

Rents have risen much faster than local incomes, leaving families unable to find homes they can afford. Residents want rental assistance and additional affordable housing. The article discusses shelter costs rather than a particular eviction procedure or land-use rule.

expected.rationale: Rents have risen much faster than local incomes, leaving families unable to find homes they can afford.

blocks.text: A place in the town where they work

Local workers say the price of housing makes it impossible to remain near their jobs. A public housing assistance proposal would lower their monthly costs. The consultation asks how to make homes affordable without claiming that every applicant is already homeless.

expected.rationale: Local workers say the price of housing makes it impossible to remain near their jobs.

blocks.text: No bed available tonight

The emergency shelter turns people away each night because every bed is occupied. People sleeping outside ask for more safe places to stay. Officials are considering an expanded shelter service and longer-term support for residents who have no stable home.

expected.rationale: The emergency shelter turns people away each night because every bed is occupied.

blocks.text: Support beyond clearing the encampment

Residents living in tents say moving them from one location to another has not provided somewhere to live. Outreach workers want a coordinated response to homelessness. The report concerns people already without shelter, not simply rising rents.

expected.rationale: Residents living in tents say moving them from one location to another has not provided somewhere to live.

blocks.text: What can be built near the station?

The planning board is considering whether zoning rules should allow apartments on parcels currently restricted to detached houses. Residents can comment on the proposed land-use change. The article does not establish a transit service change or a particular rent level.

expected.rationale: The planning board is considering whether zoning rules should allow apartments on parcels currently restricted to detached houses.

blocks.text: A public decision about an empty lot

A developer wants the town to amend its land-use map so an unused commercial lot can accommodate homes. The planning hearing will consider permitted uses and building limits. Residents are invited to review the proposal before a decision is made.

expected.rationale: A developer wants the town to amend its land-use map so an unused commercial lot can accommodate homes.

blocks.text: A notice without the required process

Tenants say their landlord ordered them to leave immediately without the notice or hearing required by law. A tenants' group is asking for enforcement of eviction protections. The article centers on legal treatment of renters, not whether a new building may be constructed.

expected.rationale: Tenants say their landlord ordered them to leave immediately without the notice or hearing required by law.

blocks.text: Repairs promised, leaks left in place

Renters have repeatedly reported leaking ceilings and broken heating, but the landlord has not made repairs. They want the town to enforce habitability obligations. The request concerns tenants' right to safe homes rather than advice on household maintenance.

expected.rationale: Renters have repeatedly reported leaking ceilings and broken heating, but the landlord has not made repairs.

blocks.text: The nearest appointment is now hours away

A community clinic is closing, leaving residents unable to obtain routine medical care nearby. Patients are asking the health authority to maintain a local service. The article focuses on availability of treatment and does not attribute the closure to discrimination.

expected.rationale: A community clinic is closing, leaving residents unable to obtain routine medical care nearby.

blocks.text: Patients wait months for essential treatment

Residents describe being unable to secure medically necessary appointments because the region lacks sufficient providers. A public consultation is reviewing healthcare capacity. Their request is for timely medical care rather than changes to food assistance or grocery access.

expected.rationale: Residents describe being unable to secure medically necessary appointments because the region lacks sufficient providers.

blocks.text: Coverage promised, claim refused

Patients say their health insurance plans deny claims for treatment that their policies appear to cover. They want a review of claim procedures and benefit rules. The dispute is about medical coverage, not a general inability to afford everyday goods.

expected.rationale: Patients say their health insurance plans deny claims for treatment that their policies appear to cover.

blocks.text: A renewal backlog interrupts coverage

Families have lost Medicaid coverage while the agency processes renewal paperwork. They seek temporary coverage and clearer eligibility procedures. The public issue is continuity of health insurance, rather than a claim that a particular racial group was treated differently.

expected.rationale: Families have lost Medicaid coverage while the agency processes renewal paperwork.

blocks.text: The prevention program has too few staff

A public vaccination campaign cannot reach all eligible neighborhoods because its outreach team is understaffed. Health officials are discussing how to improve disease prevention across the population. The proposal concerns public health capacity rather than compulsory treatment of an individual.

expected.rationale: A public vaccination campaign cannot reach all eligible neighborhoods because its outreach team is understaffed.

blocks.text: Coordinating a response to an outbreak

Local public health teams are setting up testing and prevention services after an infectious disease outbreak. Residents can ask questions at an open briefing. The story concerns collective disease protection and the operation of a public health response.

expected.rationale: Local public health teams are setting up testing and prevention services after an infectious disease outbreak.

blocks.text: Nowhere to turn during a crisis

Residents seeking urgent mental health support say the community crisis service cannot answer calls overnight. The county is considering funding additional staff. The proposed action is to improve access to mental health services, not to interpret an individual's private feelings.

expected.rationale: Residents seeking urgent mental health support say the community crisis service cannot answer calls overnight.

blocks.text: Counseling places cannot meet demand

A publicly funded counseling program has a long waiting list, leaving residents without support for months. Service users are asking for expanded capacity. The article examines community mental health care and does not propose changes to school governance or insurance rules.

expected.rationale: A publicly funded counseling program has a long waiting list, leaving residents without support for months.

blocks.text: Families cannot find a preschool place

A district has fewer early-childhood learning places than eligible children. Families want an expansion so attendance is not limited by the available spaces. The issue is access to education rather than medical childcare advice or a private product comparison.

expected.rationale: A district has fewer early-childhood learning places than eligible children.

blocks.text: A second chance to learn

Adults seeking literacy classes are being turned away because the public program has no available places. Community organizers want a reliable route back into education. The article describes barriers to learning without asserting any particular group was deliberately excluded.

expected.rationale: Adults seeking literacy classes are being turned away because the public program has no available places.

blocks.text: The proposed budget removes teaching posts

The school district plans to eliminate classroom positions to close a budget gap. Families and teachers are reviewing how the education funding decision will affect students. Residents may comment before the budget is adopted.

expected.rationale: The school district plans to eliminate classroom positions to close a budget gap.

blocks.text: Who decides what the schools teach?

The school board is considering a curriculum change without its usual public consultation. Families are asking for a transparent process and a chance to speak. The report focuses on educational decision-making rather than the amount of the school budget.

expected.rationale: The school board is considering a curriculum change without its usual public consultation.

blocks.text: Suspended without a chance to respond

Students say a district disciplinary process offers no meaningful way to challenge a suspension. They are asking for notice, fair hearings and an appeal route. The public concern is students' procedural rights rather than their examination scores.

expected.rationale: Students say a district disciplinary process offers no meaningful way to challenge a suspension.

blocks.text: A school database shared too widely

Families learned that a school system had made sensitive student records available to staff who did not need them. They want clear privacy protections and oversight. The issue concerns students' rights in education, not general study skills or classroom funding.

expected.rationale: Families learned that a school system had made sensitive student records available to staff who did not need them.

blocks.text: A local plan to cut emissions

The council is considering a plan to reduce greenhouse emissions from municipal buildings and transport operations. Residents can comment on the climate targets and timetable. The article concerns climate mitigation rather than a forecast for next week's weather.

expected.rationale: The council is considering a plan to reduce greenhouse emissions from municipal buildings and transport operations.

blocks.text: Preparing neighborhoods for hotter summers

A city climate adaptation plan proposes shade and cooling measures as extreme heat becomes more frequent. Community members are reviewing which areas should receive investment first. The central issue is preparation for climate change, with no medical treatment dispute described.

expected.rationale: A city climate adaptation plan proposes shade and cooling measures as extreme heat becomes more frequent.

blocks.text: Smoke drifts across the neighborhood

Residents report repeated industrial emissions entering their homes and want stronger pollution controls. The regulator is considering enforcement against the plant. The public problem is environmental contamination even though the article mentions possible respiratory effects.

expected.rationale: Residents report repeated industrial emissions entering their homes and want stronger pollution controls.

blocks.text: A habitat faces permanent loss

A proposed development would remove a protected wetland used by local wildlife. Conservation groups are seeking a review of the environmental decision. Their concern is preserving habitat, not the cost or tenancy rules of the proposed buildings.

expected.rationale: A proposed development would remove a protected wetland used by local wildlife.

blocks.text: Residents face losing their water supply

Households unable to pay their water bills have received shutoff notices. A community group wants affordable access to drinking water and a review of utility policy. The article focuses on the water system rather than food supplies or medical insurance.

expected.rationale: Households unable to pay their water bills have received shutoff notices.

blocks.text: A system that cannot reliably deliver water

Frequent failures in the public water network leave homes without a dependable supply. Residents are asking for repairs and a transparent investment plan. The concern is reliable access to drinking water, not a diagnosis of individual health conditions.

expected.rationale: Frequent failures in the public water network leave homes without a dependable supply.

blocks.text: The last bus may disappear

The transit agency proposes canceling an evening bus route used by residents returning from work. Passengers want the service retained and have organized comments for the public hearing. The article concerns public transit provision rather than a private driving itinerary.

expected.rationale: The transit agency proposes canceling an evening bus route used by residents returning from work.

blocks.text: Longer gaps between trains

Commuters say proposed rail service reductions would make the regional system unreliable. The agency is inviting feedback on its schedule and funding plan. Residents want frequent public transit without the report making a separate claim about disability discrimination.

expected.rationale: Commuters say proposed rail service reductions would make the regional system unreliable.

blocks.text: A dangerous crossing outside the library

Neighbors have documented repeated near misses where people cross a busy road. They are asking for a safer crossing and lower vehicle speeds. The request concerns pedestrian safety and street design rather than police powers or criminal sentencing.

expected.rationale: Neighbors have documented repeated near misses where people cross a busy road.

blocks.text: A bridge needs more than another patch

Engineers say a public bridge requires major repairs to remain usable. The local authority is consulting residents about its infrastructure investment plan. The issue is maintenance of a transportation asset rather than rules for building housing nearby.

expected.rationale: Engineers say a public bridge requires major repairs to remain usable.

blocks.text: Essential trips require a car people do not have

Residents without cars cannot reach jobs and public services using available transportation. A community consultation is examining options for practical access. The issue is mobility and access to destinations, not a claim that the services themselves refuse to help residents.

expected.rationale: Residents without cars cannot reach jobs and public services using available transportation.

blocks.text: A village left outside the network

People in outlying settlements describe being unable to travel to essential destinations without relying on neighbors. The transport authority is reviewing coverage gaps. Residents seek a dependable way to get around rather than information about recreational road trips.

expected.rationale: People in outlying settlements describe being unable to travel to essential destinations without relying on neighbors.

blocks.text: Workers ask to negotiate together

Employees have formed a union and are asking their employer to recognize it as their bargaining representative. They want a collective process for negotiating workplace decisions. The story is about organizing rights rather than an announced amount of a pay increase.

expected.rationale: Employees have formed a union and are asking their employer to recognize it as their bargaining representative.

blocks.text: A seat at the negotiating table

A bargaining unit says management is making workplace changes without negotiations. Members are considering collective action to obtain a meaningful negotiating process. Their immediate demand is recognition of their representative role, not a specific medical benefit or housing policy.

expected.rationale: A bargaining unit says management is making workplace changes without negotiations.

blocks.text: The warehouse offers no relief from dangerous heat

Staff describe working in extreme heat without adequate breaks, water or protection. They want the safety regulator to enforce safe working conditions. The report concerns hazards at work even though heat illness is mentioned as a consequence.

expected.rationale: Staff describe working in extreme heat without adequate breaks, water or protection.

blocks.text: Tomorrow's schedule arrives tonight

Workers receive shifts with almost no notice and are penalized when they cannot rearrange their lives immediately. They are seeking predictable scheduling protections. The story centers on working conditions, without a dispute about the amount of wages paid.

expected.rationale: Workers receive shifts with almost no notice and are penalized when they cannot rearrange their lives immediately.

blocks.text: Keeping a job while caring for a newborn

Employees have asked lawmakers for protected parental leave so they do not risk dismissal when caring for a new child. The proposal concerns employment leave. It does not discuss abortion services or whether healthcare providers are available.

expected.rationale: Employees have asked lawmakers for protected parental leave so they do not risk dismissal when caring for a new child.

blocks.text: Staying home sick should not mean losing a job

Workers say they are expected to attend shifts while ill because they have no protected sick leave. They are asking for employment protections. Although illness motivates the request, the policy at issue concerns time away from work rather than access to treatment.

expected.rationale: Workers say they are expected to attend shifts while ill because they have no protected sick leave.

blocks.text: People seeking refuge need help with their claims

A community organization cannot meet demand for advice from asylum seekers navigating protection procedures. Volunteers are seeking support for the service. The article concerns access to the asylum process rather than ordinary tourism or vacation planning.

expected.rationale: A community organization cannot meet demand for advice from asylum seekers navigating protection procedures.

blocks.text: Arriving safely is only the beginning

A resettlement program helps newly arrived refugees find their way through local services. Its organizers are asking for volunteers and reliable funding. The public issue is support for people seeking refuge, without identifying a separate housing shortage or medical dispute.

expected.rationale: A resettlement program helps newly arrived refugees find their way through local services.

blocks.text: Families ask for a fair hearing before removal

Residents facing deportation say they have little opportunity to present their cases before removal proceeds. Advocates want immigration procedures reviewed. The story centers on removal policy rather than an unrelated criminal prosecution.

expected.rationale: Residents facing deportation say they have little opportunity to present their cases before removal proceeds.

blocks.text: An immigration detention decision with no clear review

People held pending immigration decisions say they cannot obtain an explanation or timely review of continued detention. A public inquiry is considering procedural protections. The central issue is immigration enforcement and detention, not ordinary prison sentencing.

expected.rationale: People held pending immigration decisions say they cannot obtain an explanation or timely review of continued detention.

blocks.text: Citizenship applications wait for years

Applicants who have completed the requirements for naturalization cannot obtain decisions because of a processing backlog. They are asking the agency to address the delay. The report concerns access to citizenship procedures rather than the management of polling stations.

expected.rationale: Applicants who have completed the requirements for naturalization cannot obtain decisions because of a processing backlog.

blocks.text: Essential assistance depends on immigration status

A local policy bars undocumented residents from a general assistance service offered to other residents in the same circumstances. Community groups seek equal access regardless of status. The article identifies a status-based barrier without attributing it to race or medical eligibility.

expected.rationale: A local policy bars undocumented residents from a general assistance service offered to other residents in the same circumstances.

blocks.text: Voting hours exclude people on long shifts

Residents say the limited hours at polling places make it difficult to cast a ballot after work. They are asking election officials to extend access. The concern is the ability to vote, not whether the workplace should change its schedules.

expected.rationale: Residents say the limited hours at polling places make it difficult to cast a ballot after work.

blocks.text: Registration has an unnecessary barrier

Eligible voters report being turned away from registration because officials demand documents not required by the published rules. A civic group wants the procedure corrected. The report focuses on ballot access rather than citizenship applications.

expected.rationale: Eligible voters report being turned away from registration because officials demand documents not required by the published rules.

blocks.text: Observers ask how ballots are counted

Election administrators are holding a public briefing on counting procedures, audits and poll-worker training. Residents can ask how the process is checked. The article concerns election administration and does not assert that particular voters were denied access.

expected.rationale: Election administrators are holding a public briefing on counting procedures, audits and poll-worker training.

blocks.text: A neighborhood divided between districts

Proposed electoral district lines split a community among several constituencies. Residents say this weakens their representation and want the boundary commission to reconsider. The issue is how people are represented, not the opening hours of polling locations.

expected.rationale: Proposed electoral district lines split a community among several constituencies.

blocks.text: A public contract without public records

Residents have requested documents explaining how a municipal contract was awarded, but the council has not released them. They want transparency and independent oversight. The public concern is accountable government rather than the quality of a private purchase.

expected.rationale: Residents have requested documents explaining how a municipal contract was awarded, but the council has not released them.

blocks.text: Decisions announced after the doors close

A council makes important decisions in meetings residents cannot observe or review. Community members are asking for accessible agendas, records and public scrutiny. The issue is government accountability rather than a specific school curriculum or health service.

expected.rationale: A council makes important decisions in meetings residents cannot observe or review.

blocks.text: Complaints need an independent hearing

Residents say complaints about police conduct are reviewed only by the same department involved. They are asking for independent oversight and transparent findings. The article focuses on policing accountability without identifying race as the basis of the conduct.

expected.rationale: Residents say complaints about police conduct are reviewed only by the same department involved.

blocks.text: Returning home without a route to support

People leaving prison describe gaps in reentry support that make rebuilding everyday life difficult. A community group wants a coordinated public response. The story concerns the consequences of incarceration rather than immigration removal procedures.

expected.rationale: People leaving prison describe gaps in reentry support that make rebuilding everyday life difficult.

blocks.text: A court process residents cannot navigate

People representing themselves in civil court say forms and procedures are impossible to understand without assistance. They seek legal aid and a fair opportunity to be heard. The article is about access to justice rather than a particular housing or immigration claim.

expected.rationale: People representing themselves in civil court say forms and procedures are impossible to understand without assistance.

blocks.text: Preventing conflict before another person is hurt

A neighborhood program intervenes in disputes before they become violent, but its funding is ending. Residents want support for community violence prevention. No firearm law or change in police powers is proposed in the article.

expected.rationale: A neighborhood program intervenes in disputes before they become violent, but its funding is ending.

blocks.text: Lawmakers debate firearm background checks

A legislative committee is reviewing a proposal to strengthen background checks for firearm purchases. Residents are invited to give evidence about gun policy. The issue is regulation of firearms rather than weapons in a game or a historical collection.

expected.rationale: A legislative committee is reviewing a proposal to strengthen background checks for firearm purchases.

blocks.text: Families ask for an inspection of the jail

Families report unsafe conditions and prolonged isolation in the local jail. They want an independent inspection and changes in how people are held. The report concerns conditions of incarceration rather than a proposal about immigration detention.

expected.rationale: Families report unsafe conditions and prolonged isolation in the local jail.

blocks.text: Care is available only across a state border

Residents seeking abortions must travel long distances because local services are legally restricted. A support group is organizing practical assistance and advocating changes to access rules. The central issue is abortion access, not a generic insurance claim.

expected.rationale: Residents seeking abortions must travel long distances because local services are legally restricted.

blocks.text: A restriction would close the remaining service

A proposed rule would prevent the area's remaining abortion provider from operating. Residents can comment before the rule is adopted. The article addresses availability of abortion services rather than general hospital funding or contraception advice.

expected.rationale: A proposed rule would prevent the area's remaining abortion provider from operating.

blocks.text: A policy narrows access to contraceptives

Public clinics may stop offering contraceptives under a proposed funding condition. Residents are asking officials to maintain affordable access. The concern is access to contraception, not a debate about whether unrelated medical treatments are covered by insurance.

expected.rationale: Public clinics may stop offering contraceptives under a proposed funding condition.

blocks.text: A reproductive decision made without consent

Patients describe being sterilized without meaningful informed consent and are seeking protections against reproductive coercion. The public inquiry concerns bodily autonomy and reproductive decisions. It does not establish a separate insurance or clinic-capacity issue.

expected.rationale: Patients describe being sterilized without meaningful informed consent and are seeking protections against reproductive coercion.

blocks.text: Diabetes appears in the leaflet, hunger is the problem

The food bank cannot supply enough groceries for the households waiting outside. Families describe empty cupboards and skipping meals. A volunteer mentions diabetes and public health in a nutrition leaflet, but residents are asking for enough food, not medical care or a new health service.

expected.rationale: The food bank cannot supply enough groceries for the households waiting outside.

blocks.text: Equal symptoms, unequal treatment

Black patients describe being repeatedly denied referrals that white patients with the same symptoms receive. The report identifies race-based treatment and asks the hospital to change its practices. Those denied referrals also cannot obtain the medical care they need.

expected.rationale: Black patients describe being repeatedly denied referrals that white patients with the same symptoms receive.

blocks.text: Pain dismissed because the patient is a woman

Women say clinicians routinely dismiss their symptoms while offering investigations to men with comparable complaints. An equality review found evidence supporting their accounts. They seek an end to discriminatory treatment and timely access to the medical care being withheld.

expected.rationale: Women say clinicians routinely dismiss their symptoms while offering investigations to men with comparable complaints.

blocks.text: The pantry is open but the bus no longer runs

Families who depend on the community pantry cannot collect groceries after the bus route serving it was canceled. They report missing meals and ask for emergency food deliveries. Organizers also want the transit agency to restore the route that connected them to food assistance.

expected.rationale: Families who depend on the community pantry cannot collect groceries after the bus route serving it was canceled.

blocks.text: Renters face different rules because of race

Black tenants say their landlord threatens eviction for conduct tolerated from white tenants. An investigation found unequal enforcement of the same lease terms. Residents want protection from racial discrimination and enforcement of lawful tenant procedures.

expected.rationale: Black tenants say their landlord threatens eviction for conduct tolerated from white tenants.

blocks.text: The bus arrives, but wheelchair users cannot board

The transit operator keeps using vehicles with broken wheelchair lifts and offers no equivalent alternative. Disabled residents want equal access to the service. They are also asking for a reliable, accessible public bus operation rather than treatment for a medical condition.

expected.rationale: The transit operator keeps using vehicles with broken wheelchair lifts and offers no equivalent alternative.

blocks.text: Health insurance brochures do not fill a cupboard

A charity hands out donated groceries alongside information about health insurance and medical care. Its urgent appeal is to replenish food supplies because families are going hungry. The article identifies no coverage dispute and no obstacle to receiving medical treatment.

expected.rationale: A charity hands out donated groceries alongside information about health insurance and medical care.

blocks.text: Missing pay means missing meals

Workers whose employer withheld earned wages cannot buy enough groceries for their children. Their main demand is recovery of the stolen pay through enforcement action. The report also documents food insecurity and the need for emergency food assistance while claims are processed.

expected.rationale: Workers whose employer withheld earned wages cannot buy enough groceries for their children.

blocks.text: Affordable homes need protection from flooding

Residents seek affordable housing after repeated displacement made local rents unaffordable. The proposed housing program would also adapt homes to worsening climate-related flooding. The central request is access to affordable homes, with climate adaptation an explicit second objective.

expected.rationale: Residents seek affordable housing after repeated displacement made local rents unaffordable.

blocks.text: An emissions plan must include displaced workers

The government is proposing to phase out a high-emissions industry to meet climate targets. The report primarily examines the emissions policy, but also documents job losses and calls for retraining workers who would become unemployed. Both problems are substantively discussed.

expected.rationale: The government is proposing to phase out a high-emissions industry to meet climate targets.

blocks.text: A food program excludes undocumented families

Families unable to afford groceries are going hungry because a public food program excludes residents without specified immigration documents. The main appeal is for access to food assistance. Organizers also challenge the immigration-status condition that prevents these families from receiving help.

expected.rationale: Families unable to afford groceries are going hungry because a public food program excludes residents without specified immigration documents.

blocks.text: Lunch portions shrink when the budget does

Children who rely on school meals report going hungry after the district reduced its meal program. Families primarily want dependable access to food. The article also examines the school budget decision that removed funding from the meal service.

expected.rationale: Children who rely on school meals report going hungry after the district reduced its meal program.

blocks.text: A crisis response beyond police dispatch

Residents want a staffed mental health crisis team because no clinical response is available overnight. They also question the police department's current practice of treating those calls as enforcement incidents. The proposal prioritizes crisis care and separately changes policing procedures.

expected.rationale: Residents want a staffed mental health crisis team because no clinical response is available overnight.

blocks.text: Same work, unequal pay

Women doing the same work with the same experience are paid less than men, according to a workplace audit. Their primary complaint is discriminatory treatment based on gender. They are also seeking recovery of the pay difference and enforcement of compensation rules.

expected.rationale: Women doing the same work with the same experience are paid less than men, according to a workplace audit.

blocks.text: A schedule used to exclude one faith

Managers consistently assign workers of one religion shifts that prevent observance while accommodating comparable requests from others. Staff seek equal religious treatment and a fair scheduling process. Both discriminatory decisions and working conditions are part of the complaint.

expected.rationale: Managers consistently assign workers of one religion shifts that prevent observance while accommodating comparable requests from others.

blocks.text: A shelter excludes people it is meant to serve

An emergency shelter turns away transgender applicants because of their identity. Those rejected remain without a safe place to sleep. The article centers on discriminatory exclusion, while also documenting unmet shelter needs among people experiencing homelessness.

expected.rationale: An emergency shelter turns away transgender applicants because of their identity.

blocks.text: An inaccessible hearing prevents a defense

A deaf defendant cannot obtain interpretation for a court hearing and therefore cannot participate on equal terms. Advocates focus on disability accommodations. The report also raises a substantive access-to-justice problem because the hearing would proceed without a meaningful opportunity to respond.

expected.rationale: A deaf defendant cannot obtain interpretation for a court hearing and therefore cannot participate on equal terms.

blocks.text: Doctors are quoted, but the demand is repairs

Tenants ask the city to enforce repairs after landlords ignored leaking ceilings and broken heating. A doctor explains that cold and damp can affect public health. The story does not identify a shortage of medical care; the requested action is enforcement of tenant protections.

expected.rationale: Tenants ask the city to enforce repairs after landlords ignored leaking ceilings and broken heating.

blocks.text: Eligible voters cannot get through the door

A polling place is accessible only by stairs, preventing some eligible residents from casting ballots. The story primarily concerns voting access. Disabled voters also seek accommodations and equal treatment so the same barrier does not recur at the next election.

expected.rationale: A polling place is accessible only by stairs, preventing some eligible residents from casting ballots.

blocks.text: Outreach needs to reach every neighborhood

A vaccination program lacks enough staff to serve several neighborhoods during an outbreak. The article lists the racial composition of those neighborhoods but offers no evidence of unequal treatment based on race. Its substantive proposal is expanded public health outreach and disease prevention.

expected.rationale: A vaccination program lacks enough staff to serve several neighborhoods during an outbreak.

blocks.text: A rent crisis prompts a land-use proposal

Families priced out of local rentals ask for more affordable housing. The council proposes allowing additional apartments by changing zoning rules. The article centers on shelter affordability and separately discusses the land-use change intended to address it.

expected.rationale: Families priced out of local rentals ask for more affordable housing.

blocks.text: Safe water and an outbreak response

The main report concerns a failing water system that cannot reliably supply safe drinking water. Public health teams have also begun a disease-prevention response after illnesses were linked to the failure. Residents seek both water-system repairs and the described public health intervention.

expected.rationale: The main report concerns a failing water system that cannot reliably supply safe drinking water.

blocks.text: No leave means no chance to attend treatment

Workers seek protected leave because they risk dismissal for attending medically necessary appointments. The article primarily examines employment leave rules. It also documents residents being unable to obtain needed medical care because the appointments conflict with mandatory shifts.

expected.rationale: Workers seek protected leave because they risk dismissal for attending medically necessary appointments.

blocks.text: An enforcement policy with race-based targeting

The main proposal under debate expands deportation enforcement. A documented review also finds officers selecting people for checks based on race rather than relevant evidence. The article addresses both immigration removal policy and discriminatory enforcement practices.

expected.rationale: The main proposal under debate expands deportation enforcement.

blocks.text: People in jail are not getting enough to eat

An inspection of jail conditions reports that meals are regularly inadequate and people are going hungry. Its primary focus is conditions of incarceration and institutional accountability. The report also explicitly identifies unreliable access to sufficient food for those detained.

expected.rationale: An inspection of jail conditions reports that meals are regularly inadequate and people are going hungry.

blocks.text: A surplus on farms, empty cupboards in town

A cooperative proposes distributing unsold produce to residents who cannot afford groceries. The appeal centers on hunger and access to enough food. Although farms and healthy eating are mentioned, the article presents no climate-policy dispute or medical treatment problem.

expected.rationale: A cooperative proposes distributing unsold produce to residents who cannot afford groceries.

blocks.text: A bus consultation includes a hospital stop

The transit agency plans to cancel a route whose destinations include a hospital, library and shopping district. Passengers want the public transit service retained. Healthcare access is not separately investigated, and the article does not claim medical treatment is being denied.

expected.rationale: The transit agency plans to cancel a route whose destinations include a hospital, library and shopping district.

blocks.text: An equality audit of a community program

A nutrition education program rejects otherwise eligible Black applicants while accepting comparable white applicants. The central complaint is racial discrimination in admission. The report mentions diabetes and health insurance in describing the curriculum, but identifies neither food deprivation nor a medical-service problem.

expected.rationale: A nutrition education program rejects otherwise eligible Black applicants while accepting comparable white applicants.

blocks.text: Coverage rules block contraceptive access

Residents cannot afford prescribed contraception because their health insurance excludes it. The article's central demand is access to contraceptives. It also directly challenges the insurance benefit rule, rather than merely mentioning that medical services generally cost money.

expected.rationale: Residents cannot afford prescribed contraception because their health insurance excludes it.

blocks.text: Residents seek the records behind a school decision

A public records campaign asks officials to release documents they withheld about a school curriculum decision. The article primarily examines government transparency. It also explains that the school board bypassed its consultation process, making educational governance a substantive secondary issue.

expected.rationale: A public records campaign asks officials to release documents they withheld about a school curriculum decision.

blocks.text: This was not fair

People in the comments say the decision was unfair, but the post never identifies the decision, the institution involved or what happened. There is not enough evidence to determine whether this concerns a civic issue, a private disagreement or a misunderstanding.

expected.rationale: People in the comments say the decision was unfair, but the post never identifies the decision, the institution involved or what happened.

blocks.text: The numbers differ

A chart shows different outcomes for two unnamed groups. No source, explanation or treatment process is supplied. The accompanying text asks whether the difference matters, without establishing discrimination, a medical problem or any public action that could address it.

expected.rationale: A chart shows different outcomes for two unnamed groups.

blocks.text: Our service is changing

The notice says a service will change next month but does not say what service it is or who provides it. Several readers are worried. Nothing in the available text establishes a particular civic problem or an appropriate issue category.

expected.rationale: The notice says a service will change next month but does not say what service it is or who provides it.

blocks.text: Only a reply remains

The visible reply says that the policy could hurt people and should be challenged. The original post is unavailable. There is no description of the policy, the people affected or the institution responsible, so its civic topic cannot be identified reliably.

expected.rationale: The visible reply says that the policy could hurt people and should be challenged.

blocks.text: They should do something about this

A short discussion asks unnamed officials to take action about an unspecified situation. A place name appears in the account's profile but not in the post's claim. The visible content does not establish what happened or where the issue occurred.

expected.rationale: A short discussion asks unnamed officials to take action about an unspecified situation.

blocks.text: Several unrelated posts share the screen

The feed shows equally prominent snippets about a concert, a clinic and a council meeting. None is selected or expanded, and each is too brief to establish a substantive problem. There is no clear focal post to analyze as the user's current content.

expected.rationale: The feed shows equally prominent snippets about a concert, a clinic and a council meeting.

blocks.text: A phrase without its context

The page repeats a quote about freedom and fairness without identifying its speaker, subject or setting. Readers disagree about what it might mean. The available text does not establish a concrete civic problem or support any particular taxonomy label.

expected.rationale: The page repeats a quote about freedom and fairness without identifying its speaker, subject or setting.

blocks.text: An allegation without a described basis

A post alleges discrimination but provides no information about the conduct, affected people or basis of the allegation. The reply thread is unrelated. The content may concern a civic issue, but it does not support selecting a specific discrimination category or another confident label.

expected.rationale: A post alleges discrimination but provides no information about the conduct, affected people or basis of the allegation.

blocks.text: Loading
Loading.

expected.rationale: The page contains only a loading message or an announcement without substantive content.

blocks.text: Community update
Details will follow.

expected.rationale: The page contains only a loading message or an announcement without substantive content.

blocks.text: A lentil soup recipe

This cooking guide explains how to simmer lentils with vegetables and seasoning. A note discusses nutrition and serving suggestions for readers managing diabetes. It presents no difficulty obtaining food, no healthcare service barrier and no public policy or collective action question.

expected.rationale: This cooking guide explains how to simmer lentils with vegetables and seasoning.

blocks.text: A personal exercise routine

The author describes their weekly walks, stretches and preferred workout music. They explain how the routine helps them relax after work. The page offers personal lifestyle suggestions without discussing public services, rights, access barriers or a collective civic problem.

expected.rationale: The author describes their weekly walks, stretches and preferred workout music.

blocks.text: A fictional city in a strategy game

In this video game review, the player builds affordable housing and manages public health inside a simulated city. The writer evaluates graphics, pacing and game mechanics. No actual housing proposal, health service or real-world civic problem is discussed.

expected.rationale: In this video game review, the player builds affordable housing and manages public health inside a simulated city.

blocks.text: Running background workers in a queue

This software tutorial explains how worker processes take jobs from a queue and retry failed tasks. It uses examples involving job priority and resource limits. The words workers and jobs refer to computer processes rather than employment or labor conditions.

expected.rationale: This software tutorial explains how worker processes take jobs from a queue and retry failed tasks.

blocks.text: Paper decorations for a classroom

A craft guide shows teachers how to fold paper decorations with students. It lists materials, colors and assembly steps. There is no discussion of school funding, curriculum governance, unequal access or student rights; the page is an activity tutorial.

expected.rationale: A craft guide shows teachers how to fold paper decorations with students.

blocks.text: A weekend of sightseeing

A travel diary describes visiting museums, eating lunch and enjoying views of London. The writer mentions taking a bus as part of the trip. It contains no dispute about transit provision, rights or local public policy and asks for no civic action.

expected.rationale: A travel diary describes visiting museums, eating lunch and enjoying views of London.

blocks.text: A holiday apartment with a view

This listing advertises a furnished apartment for a short holiday stay. It describes the balcony, kitchen and nearby restaurants, then provides booking instructions. It does not establish housing insecurity, unfair tenant treatment or a public affordability problem.

expected.rationale: This listing advertises a furnished apartment for a short holiday stay.

blocks.text: Vocabulary for a language lesson

A language workbook asks readers to translate the words health insurance, hospital, public health and medical care. The page is a vocabulary exercise, not a report about access to treatment, insurance eligibility or a civic health policy question.

expected.rationale: A language workbook asks readers to translate the words health insurance, hospital, public health and medical care.

blocks.text: A novel about an imagined election

The review describes a fictional election and a character's struggle over voting rights in an invented country. Its focus is narrative structure and prose. It does not present an actual election-access problem or invite participation in a current civic issue.

expected.rationale: The review describes a fictional election and a character's struggle over voting rights in an invented country.

blocks.text: Union types in a programming language

The tutorial explains how a union type can represent several alternative values. It shows examples of narrowing and type checking. Union is a programming term here, with no reference to collective bargaining, worker representation or a public labor dispute.

expected.rationale: The tutorial explains how a union type can represent several alternative values.

blocks.text: Choosing equipment in a video game

A game guide compares virtual firearms and discusses which equipment works best in different levels. The author evaluates fictional damage scores and movement speed. No real firearm regulation, gun violence policy or community safety problem is discussed.

expected.rationale: A game guide compares virtual firearms and discusses which equipment works best in different levels.

blocks.text: A family holiday bread

The writer shares a bread recipe made for a religious holiday, explaining ingredients and family traditions. No person is excluded from a service or treated unfairly because of belief. The page concerns cooking and observance rather than religious discrimination.

expected.rationale: The writer shares a bread recipe made for a religious holiday, explaining ingredients and family traditions.

blocks.text: Grammatical gender in a language course

A lesson explains how nouns take different grammatical genders and how articles agree with them. Examples concern household objects and animals. It does not discuss unequal treatment of people, workplace rules or gender-based exclusion from public life.

expected.rationale: A lesson explains how nouns take different grammatical genders and how articles agree with them.

blocks.text: Comparing two wheelchair accessories

The reviewer compares the fit and comfort of two commercially available wheelchair cushions. They describe their personal preferences and purchase experience. No access barrier, denied accommodation or discriminatory rule is identified in the review.

expected.rationale: The reviewer compares the fit and comfort of two commercially available wheelchair cushions.

blocks.text: Tomorrow's local weather

The forecast predicts rain in the morning and clearer skies in the afternoon. It advises carrying an umbrella and checking conditions before a walk. It makes no claim about climate change, public adaptation measures or environmental regulation.

expected.rationale: The forecast predicts rain in the morning and clearer skies in the afternoon.

blocks.text: Painting reflections in water

An art tutorial demonstrates watercolor techniques for painting a lake and reflections. It explains brush pressure, pigment and drying time. Water is the subject of the painting, not a public utility, conservation dispute or drinking-water access problem.

expected.rationale: An art tutorial demonstrates watercolor techniques for painting a lake and reflections.

blocks.text: How I prepared for an interview

The author shares personal suggestions for researching a company and practicing answers before a job interview. No hiring exclusion, mass job loss or public employment policy is discussed. The page provides individual career advice without establishing a civic problem.

expected.rationale: The author shares personal suggestions for researching a company and practicing answers before a job interview.

blocks.text: A quiet evening and a journal

The writer reflects on feeling tired, listening to music and writing in a notebook. They describe a personal way to unwind. The post contains no mental health service barrier, community crisis program or public policy claim.

expected.rationale: The writer reflects on feeling tired, listening to music and writing in a notebook.

blocks.text: Fans vote for their favorite goal

A sports site asks readers to vote in an entertainment poll about the best goal of the season. It describes highlights and player reactions. This is not voter registration, an election for public office or a democratic participation barrier.

expected.rationale: A sports site asks readers to vote in an entertainment poll about the best goal of the season.

blocks.text: Designing a logo for a fictional food bank

A graphic-design exercise asks students to invent a logo for an imaginary food bank. It discusses shapes, color and typography. The fictional brief does not establish real hunger, unavailable groceries or an actual volunteering opportunity.

expected.rationale: A graphic-design exercise asks students to invent a logo for an imaginary food bank.

blocks.text: Does anyone know a place that can help tonight?

I used the last tin of beans for the children and there is nothing left until my wages arrive on Friday. Several families on our street are in the same position. We are asking the community center to organize a dependable grocery pickup rather than occasional parcels.

expected.rationale: I used the last tin of beans for the children and there is nothing left until my wages arrive on Friday.

blocks.text: They asked only the women about becoming parents

Everyone shortlisted had the same experience. The interview panel asked the women whether they planned to have children, rejected them as a risk and selected less experienced men. Staff are asking the employer to stop using those questions and review the decisions fairly.

expected.rationale: Everyone shortlisted had the same experience.

blocks.text: The parking lot is not a place to live

We have been sleeping in our car since losing our last place. Every shelter we call says it is full, and other families here have heard the same answer. We are asking the town for somewhere safe to stay while longer-term homes are arranged.

expected.rationale: We have been sleeping in our car since losing our last place.

blocks.text: The only local surgery has shut its doors

The practice where residents received their regular treatment closed last month and no replacement has opened. People cannot obtain appointments elsewhere because the other practices are full. They are asking the regional authority to restore a local service rather than sending them away again.

expected.rationale: The practice where residents received their regular treatment closed last month and no replacement has opened.
